# Oriole Scheduling — Continuity and restoration standard

Version 1.0. Effective 1 September 2026.

This standard defines the three supplier obligations reviewed for the named service. Descriptions of internal filing and contacts do not create additional supplier duties. Evidence is assessed as of 17 September 2026; an exception applies only where its conditions are documented.

## 1. Recovery commitments

For a high-criticality service, the supplier must contractually commit to recovery within 7 hours of declaring a service disruption and to losing no more than 3 hours of committed customer transactions.

## 2. Annual restoration exercise

For a high-criticality service, the supplier must perform a restoration exercise at least once every 12 months and provide a dated result covering the contracted production configuration.

## 3. Exercise remediation

Each unresolved material failure in the supplied restoration exercise must have a documented corrective action and target date. A successful exercise with no material failures does not require a remediation plan.

# Beacon Orchard — Service assurance packet

Statement date: 17 September 2026. Scope: the contracted customer service described below.

The signed service schedule commits to restoration within 5 hours after declaration of a service disruption and loss of no more than 2 hours of committed customer transactions.

Restoration exercise record RS-26 is dated 8 August 2026 and covers the contracted production configuration. The previous exercise was 20 August 2025; the next exercise is scheduled within 12 months. The result records successful recovery of every tested production dependency and no material failures.

### Beacon Orchard administrative register 001: capacity planning

Record S13-OP-101 describes the capacity planning workstream for the high-criticality scheduling service. The service directory associates this workstream with internal team 1 and release cohort 1. A coordinator compares the open work list with the preceding release summary and records items awaiting another team. The directory distinguishes a production service identifier from a training-workspace identifier; labels in screenshots are illustrative and do not expand contractual scope. This entry records 2 unresolved administrative items and 3 closed items, with a reference to meeting note S13-MN-201. Scheduling information supports delivery planning and is not evidence of security approval. The appended worksheet describes ordinary service administration; it makes no statement about backup encryption, customer authorization for data exports or export-record retention. The next register entry covers release scheduling, with separate owners and work references.

# Larkspur Scheduling — Service assurance packet

Statement date: 17 September 2026. Scope: the contracted customer service described below.

A marketing page advertises typical recovery in 2 hours, but the signed service schedule disclaims a binding recovery deadline and permits loss of up to 6 hours of committed customer transactions.

The supplied restoration record is dated 1 February 2024; its scope is the contracted production configuration. The supplier confirms that no later exercise has been performed.

That exercise contains unresolved material failure F-9. The action log says to redesign the restore dependency order, but leaves the completion-date field unassigned.
